questions.question:
**Directions: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Every boy and every girl in this class pursue at least one hobby.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'in this class pursue'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the **form of the verb 'pursue'** is **incorrect**.
 
• The **noun** that comes **after** '**Every**' is in the **singular form**.
 
• When you use ''**Every + noun**'' as a **subject**, it uses a** singular verb (verb + s)**.
 
• Therefore, the **third-person singular form of the verb 'pursues'** should be used **in place of** the verb '**pursue**'.

 

Hence, the correct answer is **option 2**.

**Correct Sentence:** *Every boy and every girl **in this class pursues** at least one hobby*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• *Subjects and verbs must agree with one another in number (singular or plural).*
 
• *Thus, if a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if a subject is plural, its verb must also be plural.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select option 'No substitution'.**

Those __whom wants to play__ the game may join the group.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'who want to play'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the use of the **pronoun 'whom'** and the **third-person singular form of the verb 'wants'** is **incorrect**.
 
• The **pronoun 'whom'** is **used instead of ‘who’ as the object of a verb or preposition**.
 
• The **pronoun 'who'** should be used **in place of** the **pronoun 'whom'**.
 
• The **pronoun 'who'** is used **to introduce a clause giving further information about a person or people previously mentioned**.
 
• Also, the **plural form of the verb 'want'** should be used **in place of** the third-person singular form of the verb 'wants'.
 
• The **antecedent 'Those' of the pronoun 'who' is plural** and therefore takes **a plural verb**.

 

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Correct Sentence:** *Those **who want to play** the game may join the group*.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.**

I asked him where he had gone in his car the previous day.

options.text: I said to him, “Where have you gone in your car the previous day?”
I said to him, “Where were you going in your car yesterday?”
I said to him, “Where you went in your car yesterday?”
I said to him, “Where did you go in your car yesterday?”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **I said to him, “Where did you go in your car yesterday?”​ **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an indirect speech.
 
• The basic rules for changing or ____converting indirect speech into direct speech__:​
 __
 
• The commas and inverted commas are added, "said to'' is added, and 'asked' is removed.
 
• The question mark (?) is added in place of the full stop (.). ''**Previous day**'' becomes ''**yesterday**''.
 
• The **third-person** pronoun 'he' will be changed into the **second-person pronoun** 'you'.
 
• The given sentence is in the **past perfect tense** format (**Subject + had + V3 (gone**)** + Object**) of **indirect speech**.
 
• The past simple tense format of the WH/Information question is **RP +, + WH + did + S + V1 + rest of the sentence**.
 
 
 
• From the following rules, we get the correct sentence as- option 4.

 

​Hence, the correct sentence is *I said to him, “Where did you go in your car yesterday?”*​ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**Directions: Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Pick the option that gives their correct order.**

A. She understood my signs, and I could make her do as I wished.

B. My constant companion was Martha, our cook’s daughter.

C. We even helped in feeding the hens which crowded around the kitchen steps.

D. This pleased me greatly and we spent a lot of time together.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'BADC'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The sentence 'B' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving general information about the noun "Martha". Hence, 'B' is the first part.
 
• The pronoun "She" mentioned in the sentence 'A' refers back to the noun 'Martha' mentioned in the sentence 'B'. Hence, 'A' follows 'B'.
 
• The pronoun "we" mentioned in the sentence 'D' refers back to the "author and Martha" mentioned in the sentence 'A'. Hence, 'D' follows 'A'.
 
• The sentence 'C' is the concluding sentence. Hence, 'C' is the last sentence.

 

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences__: *My constant companion was Martha, our cook’s daughter. She understood my signs, and I could make her do as I wished. This pleased me greatly and we spent a lot of time together. We even helped in feeding the hens which crowded around the kitchen steps.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **__Hint__***

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

Perfection is sought by him in everything he does.

options.text: He is seeking perfection in everything he does.
He has sought perfection in everything he does.
He sought perfection in everything he did.
He seeks perfection in everything he does.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'He seeks perfection in everything he does'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the passive voice and 'Perfection' is the subject and 'him' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into active voice, the subject 'Perfection' of the active voice becomes the object, the object 'him' becomes the subject 'he'.
 
• The passive format "is + V₃ (sought)" should be converted into the active format "V₁ (seeks)".
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the present simple tense.

 

**Hence, the correct active voice is** *He seeks perfection in everything he does.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.**

The lockdown prevented people __to go out from__ their homes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**from going out of**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the use of the **to-****i**nfinitive 'to go' and the preposition 'from' is incorrect.
 
• The preposition 'from' should be used before the verb as the **preposition 'from'** means **as a result of something**.
 
• The **"-ing" form of the verb** is used **after a preposition**. Therefore, the gerund or present participle form of the verb 'going' should be used in place of the verb 'go'.
 
• The preposition 'of' should be used **in place of** the **preposition 'from'**.
 
• The preposition 'from' is used **for stating someone’s/something’s origin**.
 
• The preposition 'of' is used **for expressing the relationship between a part and a whole**.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct Sentence: *The lockdown prevented people **from going out of** their homes*.

questions.question:
**Direction: From four possible words you need to select the word that can be used as a substitute to the given group of words.**

An office for which no salary is paid
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **'Honorary'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'****Honorary****'** is an adjective and it means 'relating to a position that is given to someone in order to show respect and for which no payment is made'.
 
• According to the given sentence 'A person of good understanding knowledge and reasoning power', **'Honorary'** is the correct word.

Hence *option 1* is the most appropriate option here.
